deviations: Table 4: global_approval.dta has 44 countries (paper says 66); used as provided. DV is `lag_approval`, which is missing in the last quarter of every panel and so is the next-quarter (lead) approval aligned to quarter t; regressed on contemporaneous kill_16 (16+ deaths = more than 15; 60 attack quarters, 9 under women in the full file, 50 / 9 in the estimation sample).

Table 4: 'GDP' control is the `growth` variable as provided (values look like GDP levels); election control is election_qtr (the only election variable); execrlc (DPI left/center/right, 0 = no information) entered as categories; OLS with country dummies. Panel-corrected SEs do not affect point estimates and were not needed (the informational PCSE block returned NULL and printed nothing).

Table 2: OLS (likeability) and logit (best PM, log-odds coefficients, as the table note says) with wave dummies entered after `time`; the collinear last wave dummy is dropped (wave 16 for likeability, wave 12 for best PM), so `time` is identified relative to that convention. Controls white, gender, labour, party_other, income, ideology2 (midpoint-recoded ideology); listwise deletion; no survey weights. Restricting to wave-12 participants gives identical samples and estimates.
notes: Independent blind reproduction from paper text and data files only. Two exploratory runs (variable inspection; no RESULT lines), then one final run. The paper text had the target values withheld; no author scripts or result files were opened. The Readme .docx and metadata.json in the data directory were read for documentation only. Table 4 R2 from lm with dummies (0.27) differs from the R2 printed in the paper's Table 4; this was not used to change the specification.
